title: Logic
summary: Logic as the art of non-contradictory identification.

lessons.title: The art itself
lessons.objective: State logic as the art of identifying what is, and of keeping those identifications free of contradiction.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is logic?

choices.text: The art of non-contradictory identification
A feeling that a conclusion is comfortable
Whatever most people agree to call true
A word game with no tie to facts

feedback.note: Logic is an art you practice: you identify what is, and you do not let those identifications contradict one another.

exercises.prompt: Which pair names the two jobs packed into that definition?

choices.text: Identify, and keep the identifications non-contradictory
Identify quickly, and ignore later conflicts
Sound formal, and avoid everyday words
Doubt every identification, and stop there

feedback.note: Identification says what something is. Non-contradiction keeps those sayings compatible with one another and with the facts.

exercises.prompt: Match each word in the definition to the job it names.

pairs.left: Art
pairs.right: A method you can practice, not a mood

pairs.left: Identification
Non-contradictory

feedback.note: All three words belong in the definition. Drop any one and you no longer have logic as this unit uses the word.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition of logic used in this unit.

feedback.note: The standard is non-contradiction. Popularity, feeling, and a rough guess are not substitutes for it.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states what logic is.

feedback.note: Logic identifies. It does not treat agreement or wishing as the work.

exercises.prompt: Someone calls a chain of thoughts logical only because it feels tidy. What is missing?

choices.text: A check that the thoughts identify facts without contradicting them
A longer sentence and more technical words
A larger group that likes the conclusion
A faster delivery of the same feeling

feedback.note: Tidy wording is not logic. Logic is identification that does not contradict what is.

exercises.prompt: Which activity is an exercise of logic?

choices.text: Naming what a thing is, then rejecting a claim that clashes with that naming
Keeping whichever claim you like better
Accepting two claims that cannot both be true
Refusing to identify anything at all

feedback.note: You identify, then you refuse the identification that contradicts the first. That is the art in action.

exercises.prompt: Match each practice to whether it is logic.

pairs.left: Identify the facts and drop a clash
Assert two incompatible claims together
Replace identification with a wish

feedback.note: Logic stays with identification and with consistency. Wishing and contradiction leave that art.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two requirements.

parts.text: what is, and you reject a

feedback.note: Identification without a ban on contradiction is incomplete. So is a ban on contradiction if you never identify anything.

lessons.title: Identify what is
lessons.objective: Treat logic as naming facts that are already there, not as inventing them or swapping them for a wish.

exercises.prompt: What does identification do?

choices.text: It states what a thing is
It makes the thing into whatever you prefer
It hides the thing so a claim can stand
It waits for a group to decide what the thing is

feedback.note: To identify is to grasp and state the identity of something that exists. Preference and a vote do not do that work.

exercises.prompt: A cup is on the table. Which response is identification?

choices.text: The cup is on the table
I wish the cup were a book, so it is a book
It is a cup and it is not a cup, in the same respect
Nothing can be said about the cup

feedback.note: Identification reports the fact. A wish does not rewrite the cup, and a contradiction does not count as naming it.

exercises.prompt: Match each move to what it does with the facts.

pairs.left: State what the thing is
Pretend the thing is something else
Refuse to say what anything is

feedback.note: Logic begins when you name what is. Evasion and a blank refusal both skip that step.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about the work of logic.

feedback.note: The object of identification is reality. A wish is not a second kind of fact that logic must honor.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that says what identification reports.

feedback.note: The report is about the thing, not about a preference standing in for the thing.

exercises.prompt: You want the road to be dry, and it is wet. What does logic require you to identify?

choices.text: The road is wet
The road is dry, because you need it to be
Either answer, since both are identifications of a sort
Nothing, until the wish changes

feedback.note: Need does not alter the fact. Logic identifies the wet road.

exercises.prompt: Which mistake treats logic as something other than identification?

choices.text: Using a conclusion to create the facts it was supposed to name
Looking again when two reports clash
Naming a thing by the characteristics it has
Dropping a claim that contradicts a known fact

feedback.note: Identification follows the facts. It does not issue the facts so that a preferred claim can stay.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the right description.

pairs.left: The metal is cold to the touch
Calling the metal warm because you hoped it was
pairs.right: A wish in place of identification

pairs.left: Saying the metal is both cold and not cold in the same respect

feedback.note: Only the first item names what is. The second substitutes a wish. The third cancels the naming.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule for this lesson.

feedback.note: If the content is invented, the step was not identification, and it was not logic.

lessons.title: Not both at once
lessons.objective: Apply non-contradiction: the same thing cannot be two incompatible things at the same time and in the same respect.

exercises.prompt: When is a pair of claims a contradiction?

choices.text: They deny each other about the same thing, at the same time, in the same respect
They describe the same thing at two different times
They describe two different parts of one thing
They use different words for the same fact

feedback.note: Difference of time, part, or wording is not a contradiction. A contradiction is the same subject said to be and not be, in one respect at one time.

exercises.prompt: A leaf cannot be all red and all green at the same time. Why does logic reject that?

choices.text: Those are incompatible identifications of the whole leaf at one time
Red and green are unpopular colors together
Color words are too ordinary to use in logic
A leaf has no identity, so any color claim fails for that reason

feedback.note: All red and all green cannot both be the identity of that leaf at that time. Logic will not accept both.

exercises.prompt: Match each pair to its status.

pairs.left: The page is all blank and all covered in ink now
The page was blank yesterday and has ink today
The top of the page is blank and the bottom has ink

feedback.note: Non-contradiction concerns one subject in one respect at one time. Change and difference of part are still identifications.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule of non-contradiction used here.

parts.text: A thing cannot be and not be, at the same time and in the same

feedback.note: The limit is same time and same respect. A later change, or another respect, is a new identification, not a contradiction.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that rejects the double claim about the leaf.

feedback.note: The clash is about one time. A leaf that is red one day and green later is a change, not this contradiction.

exercises.prompt: You cannot have your cake and eat it too. What does that example mark?

choices.text: Two incompatible identifications of the same cake at the same time
A rule about how much dessert is polite
A recipe that failed
A cake eaten today and another baked tomorrow

feedback.note: Eaten and still there, as the same cake at the same time, cannot both be identified. That is the contradiction the saying marks.

exercises.prompt: A stone is solid in the morning and broken in the afternoon. Is that a contradiction?

choices.text: No. The identifications are of different times
Yes. A thing may never change and still be itself
Yes, but only if someone is disappointed by the change
Yes, because two words were used

feedback.note: Change across time is not a contradiction. The contradiction would be solid and broken in the same respect at the same time.

exercises.prompt: Match each incompatible pair to the thing it cannot be at once.

pairs.left: All red and all green
pairs.right: The same leaf at one time

pairs.left: A stone and a leaf
pairs.right: The same object at one time

pairs.left: Eaten and still uneaten
pairs.right: The same cake at one time

feedback.note: Each pair would cancel the identity of one subject. Logic does not identify a thing as both.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two limits that keep a difference from being a contradiction.

parts.text: Check the same time and the same
before you call two claims a

feedback.note: Without those two limits, ordinary change and ordinary difference get mislabeled as contradictions.

lessons.title: The error is in the thinking
lessons.objective: Treat a contradiction as a confession that your thinking went wrong, not as a discovery that reality contradicts itself.

exercises.prompt: You reach a contradiction. What has gone wrong?

choices.text: An error in your thinking
Reality, which sometimes contradicts itself
Language, which cannot identify anything
The facts, which should be edited to fit the contradiction

feedback.note: Arriving at a contradiction confesses an error in thinking. It does not show that the facts contradict themselves.

exercises.prompt: Two of your claims cannot both be true. What should you do first?

choices.text: Find which identification is the error
Keep both and call the clash a deeper truth
Blame reality for failing to match both claims
Decide that identification is impossible

feedback.note: The contradiction is a signal to correct the thinking. It is not a new kind of fact and not a reason to give up identifying.

exercises.prompt: Match each response to a contradiction with what it does.

pairs.left: Look for the mistaken identification
pairs.right: Treats the contradiction as an error in thinking

pairs.left: Say reality itself is contradictory
Keep both claims on purpose

feedback.note: Logic locates the error in the thinking that produced the clash, then corrects that thinking.

exercises.prompt: Complete the lesson rule.

parts.text: A contradiction you reach is an error in your

feedback.note: The confession is about thinking. The world is not the thing that failed when your claims clash.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that places the error.

feedback.note: The clash is evidence against the chain of identifications, not evidence that existence contradicts itself.

exercises.prompt: Your notes say the bridge is open and that the same bridge is closed now, in the same respect. What follows?

choices.text: At least one of those identifications is wrong
Both identifications are true because you wrote both
The bridge has no identity until the notes agree
Logic requires you to accept the clash as final

feedback.note: Open and closed, same bridge, same time, same respect, cannot both stand. One identification has to be the error.

exercises.prompt: Why is it a mistake to edit the facts so that a contradiction can remain?

choices.text: Logic identifies the facts; it does not rewrite them to protect a clash
Editing facts is fine, but only if the wording stays long
The only problem is that editing takes time
Contradictions are too rare to bother checking

feedback.note: Changing the report of the facts to save both sides of a contradiction abandons identification.

exercises.prompt: Match each discovery to the proper next step.

pairs.left: Two claims contradict
A later check removes the clash
pairs.right: The error in thinking has been corrected

pairs.left: Someone calls the clash a fact about reality

feedback.note: The proper next step is correction of the thinking. A contradiction is not left in place and renamed as reality.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

parts.text: The contradiction is an error in

feedback.note: Reality is what identification has to match. When identifications clash, the thinking is what must change.

lessons.title: Do not keep the clash
lessons.objective: Distinguish finding a contradiction, which exposes an error, from maintaining it, which gives up the mind's hold on the facts.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between arriving at a contradiction and maintaining one?

choices.text: Arriving exposes an error; maintaining keeps the error in place
They are the same act, and both are the goal of logic
Maintaining is better because it shows you can hold two ideas
Arriving blames the world, and maintaining corrects it

feedback.note: Finding the clash is the confession of an error. Keeping the clash is refusing to correct it.

exercises.prompt: Someone says both claims must stand even though they contradict. What has that person done with logic?

choices.text: Left the art of non-contradictory identification
Used logic in its strictest form
Finished the identification and stopped, correctly
Proved that the facts contradict themselves

feedback.note: To maintain a contradiction is to stop identifying without contradiction. That is an exit from logic, not a use of it.

exercises.prompt: Match each choice to its result.

pairs.left: Drop the claim that caused the clash
Keep both contradictory claims
Notice the clash and recheck the facts
pairs.right: Use the contradiction as a warning

feedback.note: The warning is useful only if you then drop the error. Keeping both claims throws the warning away.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: Arrive at a contradiction and you confess an error;
it and you refuse to correct that error.

feedback.note: Maintaining is the further step: the error is known, and it is kept anyway.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that says what maintaining a contradiction does.

feedback.note: There is no deeper truth in holding both sides. The hold itself is the failure of the art.

exercises.prompt: You discover that your conclusion contradicts a fact you already identified. Which step stays inside logic?

choices.text: Give up the conclusion or correct the earlier identification, whichever the facts require
Announce that both will be kept as a special case
Erase the fact so the conclusion can stay
Rename the clash so it no longer counts as a contradiction

feedback.note: Logic keeps the identifications that match the facts and drops the one that contradicts them. Renaming the clash does not remove it.

exercises.prompt: Why does keeping a known contradiction cut you off from the facts?

choices.text: You are no longer identifying one thing as what it is
The wording sounds less confident
Checking takes longer than asserting
Other people may disagree with your style

feedback.note: If both of two incompatible identifications stand, you have stopped saying what the thing is. Contact with that fact is what you give up.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to the right name.

pairs.left: You first notice that two claims clash
You insist on both claims after you know they clash
You withdraw the claim that does not fit the facts

feedback.note: The three stages are not the same act. Only the third returns you to the art.

exercises.prompt: Build the closing rule of the unit.

feedback.note: That is the whole art in this unit: identify what is, and do not maintain a contradiction.

exercises.prompt: Which summary fits this unit and no wider topic?

choices.text: Logic is the art of non-contradictory identification
Logic is a replacement for the senses
Logic is a count of how many people agree
Logic is the mood that follows a conclusion

feedback.note: The unit is that art: identify, refuse the contradiction, and do not keep the clash once you see it.
